title: Office Fitout Cost Newcastle: Warm Shell, Cold Shell and Finish Levels
excerpt: Compare warm and cold shells, basic to high finishes, and the costs that distort $/m². Use the calculator to begin a design-led business budget.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Office Fitout Cost Newcastle | Shells, Finishes & Calculator
metaDescription: Plan your Newcastle office fitout budget. Compare warm vs cold shell and basic, mid-level or high finishes, understand $/m² limits and use the calculator.
body:
## How much does an office fitout cost in Newcastle?

There is no reliable single price for an office fitout in Newcastle, NSW. The starting condition of the premises, extent of services work, design brief, furniture, finish level and delivery constraints all affect the total. A useful early budget is a range with written assumptions, followed by design development and project-specific pricing.

**Use square-metre pricing as a guide, not a commitment.** Furniture and mechanical services can move the headline rate substantially without changing the area. A healthy design process tests how the workplace will operate and keeps the scope aligned with the budget and the business case.

[Open the office fitout cost calculator](/resources/fitout-estimator), then use the comparisons below to identify what still needs investigation. The calculator uses illustrative stored planning allowances, not verified Newcastle market rates or a contractor quotation. Its total covers its listed modelled items, not every cost your project may require.

## What do published cost guides actually tell us?

A local reference can help frame a conversation, provided its date and scope remain visible. Evercon's Newcastle guide, published in May 2025, gives these ex-GST reference bands:

| Published specification | Published 2025 reference, ex GST | Scope described by that source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $600–$900/m² | No furniture; partitions, carpet, paint and minimal services upgrades |
| Mid-level turnkey | $1,200–$1,600/m² | Fitout, services, meeting rooms and technology readiness |
| High-end premium | $2,000–$4,000/m² | Designer finishes, technology integration and custom joinery |

These are **another provider's historical published references**, not YOS rates, independently verified current quotes, or separate warm-shell and cold-shell prices. Do not apply an assumed escalation percentage or multiply them into an approved 2026 project budget. Read the [original Evercon Newcastle guide](https://evercon.com.au/construction/office-fit-out-cost-per-m2-newcastle-2025/) for its context.

National references use different project definitions. JLL's 2026 Australia and New Zealand guide reports an Australian average of AU$3,011/m² for a moderate-style, medium-quality office fitout. That is national context, not a Newcastle quote or a direct equivalent to the local bands above. The difference is a reason to inspect the inclusions, rather than select whichever headline suits the budget.

Our calculator's allowances are a separate illustrative model. Neither the published references nor its output replaces a measured brief, a services assessment and quotations against a coordinated design.

## Warm shell versus cold shell: establish the starting line

Shell descriptions vary between landlords and proposals. Ask for an agreed handover schedule, drawings and a site inspection instead of treating the label as a complete specification. Warm shell is not a guarantee that existing services are suitable for your new layout or headcount.

| Starting condition | Typical planning interpretation, subject to confirmation | What to check before costing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm shell | Some base-building services and finishes may already be installed | Ceiling and lighting condition; mechanical capacity and zoning; fire interfaces; electrical supply; floor finish; what is usable and retained |
| Cold shell | More of the tenancy infrastructure or finishes may still need to be installed | Precise landlord delivery scope; ceilings; distribution of services; connections; amenities; tenant and landlord responsibility for each package |
| Existing fitted office | Rooms, joinery and furniture may be available for reuse | Condition, ownership, suitability, strip-out, relocation, services changes and approval implications |

Separate landlord works from tenant-funded works. An item described as provided by the landlord may still require tenant-side distribution, connection, commissioning or modification. Record the boundary and responsible party for each item.

## Compare basic, mid-level and high finishes across both shells

Finish level and shell condition are different decisions. A basic finish in a cold shell can require substantial infrastructure work. A high finish in a suitable warm shell may spend more on selected workplace features while retaining sound existing systems. There is no universal percentage uplift between shells.

| Finish brief | Warm-shell scenario | Cold-shell scenario |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic, functional | Reuse suitable services and finishes; standard products; limited changes and bespoke joinery | Establish the required infrastructure first, then use restrained finishes and standard furniture; a basic appearance does not remove services obligations |
| Mid-level, considered | Adapt the layout and services; targeted acoustic treatment; durable finishes; specified meeting spaces and furniture | Coordinate base services, rooms, finishes and furniture together; allow for the infrastructure needed to support the brief |
| High, tailored | Retain useful existing infrastructure where suitable; selectively add bespoke joinery, specialist finishes and integrated technology | Resolve the base-building requirements alongside the detailed architectural and technology brief; test specialist allowances early |

These describe scope choices, not compliance tiers or six fixed price packages. Safety, access and required approvals are not optional upgrades. Define materials, quantities and performance requirements: two proposals both labelled mid-level can be pricing different workplaces.

A mixed specification can be sensible. For example, the brief might prioritise acoustic privacy in meeting rooms and durable everyday workstations, with a more tailored client-facing area. Ask what each investment contributes to the business rather than upgrading every surface automatically.

## Why $/m² can mislead: a worked example

The calculation is simple: **included project cost ÷ agreed floor area = cost per square metre**. The difficulty is agreeing what sits in the numerator and denominator.

Consider a hypothetical 300 m² office. These rounded figures illustrate the arithmetic only; they are not a YOS estimate, Newcastle benchmark or completed client project. All values below exclude GST.

| Included cost scope | Illustrative amount | Running total | Running rate over the same 300 m² |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Defined tenant works | $300,000 | $300,000 | $1,000/m² |
| Add furniture supply and installation | $60,000 | $360,000 | $1,200/m² |
| Add a separately identified mechanical upgrade | $90,000 | $450,000 | $1,500/m² |

The office has not grown. The reported rate has increased by 50% because the counted scope changed. That does not prove the original works became more expensive or that one proposal offers poorer value. This example omits other potential costs to isolate the effect; it is not an all-in budget.

For comparison, show a clearly defined works-only subtotal, a furniture subtotal and the whole-project total. State whether each includes design, consultants, fees, contingency and GST. Use the same area basis throughout: do not compare one tenancy's usable area with another provider's different measurement without reconciling it.

## The outliers to investigate before signing off a budget

- **Mechanical services:** existing capacity, zoning, outside-air provision, controls, after-hours operation and distribution need specialist assessment. A new enclosed-room layout may change what is required even in a warm shell. Major plant work cannot be inferred from floor area alone.
- **Furniture:** headcount, shared versus assigned desks, reuse, chair specification, storage, delivery and installation change the package. Keep loose furniture separate from built-in joinery and avoid counting either twice.
- **Electrical, fire and hydraulic work:** confirm existing capacity, proposed changes, interfaces and responsibility with the appointed specialists.
- **Acoustics, rooms and technology:** enclosed-room quantities, privacy requirements and AV briefs matter more than a finish label.
- **Premises and access:** inspect the actual Newcastle site for lift and loading arrangements, landlord work rules, existing conditions and any heritage or hazardous-material questions requiring specialist advice. Do not assume every building has the same constraints.
- **Programme:** occupied-site staging, temporary accommodation, after-hours access and long-lead selections may affect the project. Test the required occupation date against actual availability.

## Use the office fitout calculator in three passes

1. **Establish the brief.** Select furniture-only or a full fitout, enter the floor area, choose the shell condition and finish level, then add workstation numbers and the available room or technology selections. Use the same inputs when comparing options.
2. **Read the breakdown.** The full-fitout model combines an area-based base allowance with selected item allowances, workstation delivery/installation and a modelled contingency. Its displayed total per m² is the model total divided by area, not just the construction base rate. Its furniture-only path covers the listed workstation package, not a complete room-by-room furniture schedule.
3. **Record the gaps.** The tool does not inspect the building or individually assess mechanical capacity, approvals, professional fees, landlord obligations, relocation or lease-exit costs. Bring the output and a list of unknowns to a scope discussion. Replace allowances with project-specific evidence before committing.

[Try the free fitout calculator](/resources/fitout-estimator). Viewing an estimate does not require submitting an enquiry. If you choose to request an emailed report, use the form within the tool. A report records the model output; it does not turn an allowance into a fixed quotation.

Do not add a mechanical or furniture package to a quote until you have checked what the base already includes. The same rule applies when a contractor develops the calculator output into a real budget: reconcile inclusions first, then replace allowances rather than stacking overlapping amounts.

## A design process that protects the business case

Begin with the operational outcome: expected attendance, tasks, customer use, privacy, storage, accessibility, growth assumptions and the period over which the business expects to use the premises. Set the available funding and the priorities the workplace must satisfy.

Then test the space. Coordinate a measured layout with the relevant services and approval advice. Compare retention, refurbishment and relocation on the same scope and time basis. Keep a decision register showing each proposed change, its cost and programme effect, and who can approve it.

At concept design, use a range and identify the major unknowns. As the design develops, confirm quantities, specifications and specialist inputs. Before procurement, seek comparable proposals against the same scope revision, resolve exclusions and document the remaining allowances and risks. Revisit the business case at each approval point.

Design development and cost planning should inform each other. A design that cannot fit the funding envelope needs a conscious scope decision; a low allowance that cannot support the operational brief needs investigation. Neither issue is solved by choosing a more attractive $/m² figure.

Show gross project cost separately from any confirmed landlord contribution and the timing of funding. Include ongoing occupancy and operational implications in the business case with your advisers. Do not treat a possible incentive as available cash or assume an investment will deliver a particular financial return.

## Budget review checklist

Before approving the next stage, record:

- The address, measured area and area definition used in every comparison.
- The agreed shell handover condition and landlord/tenant work boundaries.
- The workplace brief, room schedule, headcount and furniture reuse decisions.
- Drawing and specification revisions shared with each pricing provider.
- Design, consultants, surveys, approvals and client-side management scope.
- Building works and separately identified services assumptions or upgrades.
- Furniture, joinery, AV, delivery and installation inclusions without duplication.
- Relocation, disruption, staging and existing-lease exit obligations where relevant.
- Provisional sums, exclusions, contingency basis, GST and payment timing.
- Decisions still required, their owners, and the point at which the business case is reviewed again.

Use the [Newcastle fitout planning guide](/blog/office-fitout-newcastle-planning-checklist) and [downloadable planning pack](/guides/fitout-project-checklist.pdf) to capture the premises brief, compare proposals and track decisions. For a furniture-only budget, see our [Newcastle office furniture buying guide](/blog/office-furniture-newcastle).

## Common questions about Newcastle fitout costs

### Is a cold-shell fitout always more expensive?

It often requires more tenant infrastructure, but the shell label alone cannot establish the difference. A warm shell with unsuitable services or extensive strip-out may need substantial work too. Compare the actual handover scope, required outcome and cost responsibilities.

### Does a higher finish level mean a better workplace?

Not automatically. The useful question is whether the specification supports the people, tasks, durability and business priorities in the brief. Invest deliberately in those requirements and test alternatives through design and cost planning.

### Is furniture included in an office fitout rate?

Only if the stated scope says so. Some published rates exclude furniture; some full-project quotes include it. Ask for the furniture schedule, delivery and installation scope, and a separate subtotal before comparing.

### Can the calculator give a fixed construction price?

No. It provides an indicative model range from your selections. Site investigation, coordinated design, specialist advice and actual procurement pricing are needed to establish a project budget and contract scope.

### Can YOS help connect the design and budget?

YOS can coordinate the client brief, appointed design and specialist inputs, cost-planning conversations, decisions, procurement and handover within an agreed scope. **YOS is the client-side project manager, not the builder or head contractor.** Appropriately appointed and licensed contractors perform construction work; your appointed advisers assess planning, certification and lease matters.

[Discuss your Newcastle office fitout brief](/office-fitout) or [send your project questions](#blog-contact-form). Bring the premises information, intended use, target date, funding envelope and the uncertainties you want to resolve.
